📖 How to use

  1. Enter your current tire size: width, aspect ratio and rim diameter.
  2. Enter the new tire size you are considering.
  3. Compare overall diameter, sidewall height and circumference side by side.
  4. Check the diameter difference % and the speedometer error before buying.

❓ Frequently asked questions

How do I read a tire size like 205/55R16?

205 is the tread width in mm, 55 is the aspect ratio (sidewall height as a percentage of width), R means radial construction, and 16 is the wheel rim diameter in inches.

How is speedometer error computed?

Your speedometer is calibrated to the old tire's circumference. True speed = indicated speed × (new circumference ÷ old circumference). A larger new tire makes the speedo read low.

How much diameter change is safe?

Most manufacturers recommend staying within ±3% of the original overall diameter to keep gearing, clearance and speedometer accuracy safe.
